skill.name: Observability & Monitoring
skill.description: Implement structured logging, Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry tracing, health checks, and practical alerting guidance for Node.js services.
skill.summary: A Node.js observability guide with reusable logging, metrics, tracing, health-check, and alerting templates.
skill.author: ArieGoldkin

security_audit.summary: Static command detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences and JavaScript template literals. Environment reads configure observability components and do not access environment files or secrets. One medium-confidence privacy risk remains: the logging middleware records unfiltered query parameters and client IP addresses.

remediation.issue: Request logs include unfiltered query parameters and client IP addresses.
remediation.suggestion: Redact sensitive query keys, avoid logging raw tokens, and apply an IP minimization or hashing policy before records leave the service.

semantic_findings.title: Potential sensitive request data in logs
semantic_findings.description: The request middleware logs the full query object and client IP address. Query parameters can contain tokens or personal data and should be filtered before logging.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The middleware explicitly includes req.query and req.ip in every request-start log entry. These fields can contain sensitive values depending on application routes and logging retention.

content.value_statement: Production services need clear signals when latency, errors, and dependencies fail. This skill provides practical Node.js templates for logs, metrics, traces, health checks, and alerts.
actual_capabilities: Explains structured JSON logging with request correlation context.
Provides a Winston request-logging middleware template.
Provides Prometheus metric guidance for HTTP, database, and cache latency.
Provides an OpenTelemetry Node SDK tracing template.
Provides liveness, readiness, and startup health-check endpoints.
Provides Prometheus alert-rule examples and severity guidance.
limitations: Templates require integration with your application dependencies and deployment environment.
It does not configure a hosted monitoring backend, dashboard, or alert delivery service.
It does not validate alert thresholds against live production traffic.
Logging templates need redaction rules for application-specific sensitive data.

use_cases.title: Instrument a new Node.js service
use_cases.description: Add structured logs, HTTP metrics, tracing, and health endpoints before the first production deployment.

use_cases.title: Improve on-call signals
use_cases.description: Define service-down, error-rate, and latency alerts with clear severity levels and response expectations.

use_cases.title: Investigate a slow request path
use_cases.description: Use trace spans, request context, and latency metrics to identify where a multi-service request slows down.

prompt_templates.title: Start with logging
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add structured Winston logging to my Express service. Include request IDs and safe fields to log.

prompt_templates.title: Add service metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Prometheus metrics for an Express API with PostgreSQL and Redis. Include useful labels and latency buckets.

prompt_templates.title: Configure distributed tracing
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the OpenTelemetry tracing template for my Node.js service. Explain which resource attributes and spans I should add.

prompt_templates.title: Design production alerts
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a focused alerting plan for this service. Use error rate, latency, saturation, and dependency health. Include thresholds and noise controls.

output_examples.input: Add readiness checks for PostgreSQL and Redis.
output: A readiness endpoint that reports dependency status and latency.
A 503 response when the database is unavailable.
A degraded status when Redis is unavailable.

output_examples.input: Recommend alerts for a customer API.
output: HighErrorRate alert for sustained server errors.
HighLatency alert using a p95 latency threshold.

output_examples.input: Review this logging plan for privacy.
output: Redact tokens, passwords, and authorization headers.
Avoid raw query parameters unless allowlisted.
Define retention and access controls for logs.

best_practices: Use structured fields and correlation IDs instead of interpolated log messages.
Redact secrets and personal data before logs or traces are exported.
Start with actionable alerts and tune thresholds using real service behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not log raw authorization headers, passwords, tokens, or unfiltered query parameters.
Do not create alerts without an owner, response expectation, or noise-control rule.
Do not treat health endpoints as proof that every business dependency is healthy.

faq.question: Which observability areas does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers structured logging, metrics, distributed tracing, health checks, and alerting guidance.

faq.question: Is this limited to Node.js?
faq.answer: The provided templates target Node.js and Express, but the principles apply to other service stacks.

faq.question: Does it install Prometheus or OpenTelemetry?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation templates and guidance, not installation or hosted service setup.

faq.question: How should I protect sensitive log data?
faq.answer: Allowlist safe fields, redact sensitive keys, and avoid raw tokens, credentials, and personal data.

faq.question: Can I use a remote tracing collector?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure the OpenTelemetry exporter endpoint for your approved collector and secure its network path.

faq.question: Does it create dashboards automatically?
faq.answer: No. It identifies useful signals, but dashboard creation and validation remain your responsibility.
